Shore Tip Station is a station on Luxter Line and Abyss Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division), and is located at Los Sengas Internal Sea. Passengers may also use this station to change to Shore Tip LRT Tung Wik Line (Shore Tip Stop), Downtown Transit Sirius Line (Shore Tip Station) and SLT Line 1902 Shore Tip Stop.

Fun Facts[]

  • This station is the permanent Down Direction Terminus of Abyss Line. [2]

History[]

  • October 20 2019: This station began services alongside Luxter Line, but Abyss Line Platforms remain reserved.
  • November 9 2019: Abyss Line extends from Kong Corner Station to this station through Twin Cliffs Station and Sand Martin Checkpoint.
  • September 8 2020: Exit E is added to this station to connect to Shore Tip LRT Shore Tip Stop.
  • January 6 2021: The Luxter Line section of this station completed Second Phase IoM Sign Replacement Works.[3]
  • October 2 2024: The Station Title of this station is announced through the monthly calender.[4]

Fun Facts[]

  • Due to the Exit Distribution of this Station, both the Los Sengas Coffee and Lavatories are set outside the Gate Area of this station.
  • Despite being named Silk Pond Station, this station is further from Silk Pond than Silk Pond Vista Station.
  • This Station, along with Silk Pond Vista Station, are stations that are related to Silk Pond, and the blue color is preferred for both stations.[2] As a result, Blue Wool is used in this station due to the fact that Light Blue Wool is already used at Silk Pond Vista Station.
  • Corresponding to Silk Pond Vista Station, The Los Sengas Coffee of this station is situated at the West of this station, which enables passengers to see the Silk Pond Bridge and Silk Pond to the west.
  • In order to enable passengers to take a good look at Silk Pond, the travelling speed of trains at Silk Pond Bridge is slower than usual.

Silk Pond Vista Station is a station on East Ring Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division), and is located at Los Sengas Cometsilk.

Station Title and Soundtrack[]

  • The Station Title of this Station is Yuujou Musubi.
  • This Station features two soundtracks that belong to the album "Gleams Between the Rails".
Name of the Soundtrack Length (mm:ss)
Yuujou Musubi 01:35
Reflections of a Gentle Bond 02:14

Fun Facts[]

  • Due to the Exit Distribution of this Station, both the Los Sengas Coffee and Lavatories are set outside the Gate Area of this station.
  • A section of the Kilo Line tracks can be seen under Silk Pond near this station.
  • This Station, along with Silk Pond Station, are stations that are related to Silk Pond, and the blue color is preferred for both stations.[2] As a result, Light Blue Wool is used in this station as the light colors allude to more light recieved due to wider scenaries seen.[3]
  • Corresponding to Silk Pond Station, The Los Sengas Coffee of this station is situated at the East of this station, which enables passengers to see the Silk Pond Bridge and Silk Pond to the east.
  • In order to enable passengers to take a good look at Silk Pond, the travelling speed of trains at Silk Pond Bridge is slower than usual.

History[]

  • September 3 2017: This Station completed construction.[4]
  • September 4 2017: This station began services.
  • March 14 2024: The Station Title Banner and Station Icons of this station are added.

Silver Plateau Station is a station on Xofa Line and Fox Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division), and is located at the west edge of Los Sengas Peckern. Passengers may also use this station to change to Peckern Transit Peckern Line (Silver Plateau Station) and Cities Transit Peckern City Circular (Silver Plateau Station).

Fun Facts[]

  • This station shares structure with Peckern Transit Silver Plateau Station, and the concoruse of this station used to be shared with Peckern Transit.
  • The old concourse of this station used to be shared with Peckern Transit until the construction of the new concourse. While the north part belongs to Peckern Transit, the south part belongs to Nazca Railway. Passengers who entered the station and wants to take Fox Line had to walk through the entirety of the Xofa Line Platforms before reaching the Fox Line platforms. With a straight distance of 380m, this walking distance was almost equivalent to two Nazca Railway Standard Length platforms.
  • When Xofa Line was named Xofa Crescent, the Station Number of that line was 5A-01. However, as Xofa Crescent was renamed Xofa Line due to changes in development plans, the Station Number is now 5A-01.[5]

History[]

  • March 13 2017: The Xofa Line Platforms of this station completed construction.[6]
  • March 18 2017: This station began services. Xofa Line and Fox Line are established. (Xofa Line was named Xofa Crescent at the time.)
  • May 13 2021: Due to changes in development plans, Xofa Crescent is renamed Xofa Line, and the Station Number of Xofa Line has changed.[7]
  • July 6 2021: Nazca Railway has announced the reconstruction of the concourse of this station. The old concourse and exits would be given to Peckern Transit. The new concourse would be located beneath the Xofa Line Platforms, and all facilities would be rebuilt, including the station control room. Moreover, a new exit (Currently Exit E) would be built to connect to the Cities Transit station of the same name (which shares fare zone).
  • July 7 2021: The new concourse began construction.
  • July 8 2021: The new concourse completed construction, and the Shopper's Street of this station also began services.

Sincerity Cove Station is a station on Pegasus Line and Phoenix Line. It is operated by Nazca Railway (Los Sengas Division), and is located at Los Sengas Downtown. Passengers may also use this station to change to Stadium Line (Bonyal Estate Station) and Phantasia Metro Bonyal to Cyan Loop Line (Bonyal Lake Station).

Fun Facts[]

  • This station is one of the two stations that enables Pegasus Line to interchange with Phoenix Line (Besides of Metropolis Terminal), with the other station being Candor Plains Station, which is a sister station of this station.
  • The two roads connecting to the east side and west side of this station provides connecting bus services and taxi services respectively.

History[]

  • February 24 2022: This station began construction.
  • February 27 2022: This station completed construction.[2]
  • February 28 2022: This station began services alongside Pegasus Line. However, as Phoenix Line have yet to begin development, the Phoenix Line platforms remain reserved.
  • April 2 2023: This station completed setting up of Phoenix Line systems.
  • April 4 2023: Phoenix Line extends from Memorial Park Station to this station.

  • November 20 2024: This Station completed construction.[3]

Skyoar Line was the second line to be established in Nazca Railway Terracept Division. This line ran between Austrumcept and Mark 4, and had a total of 12 stations. It was established alongside Nut Pond Station on September 3 2012. However, on March 10 2015, Terracept Division ended operations, and this line closed down as a result.

Description[]

Skyoar Line was the second District Railway line in Terracept NR to be established. It traveled across central Terracept in an south-north orientation.

This line was represented by the Lime Color on the Nazca Railway Route Map, and was Line Number 2.

At the time of its closure, this route was 11.18 km long, with a total of 12 stations.

Fun Facts[]

  • This line is the only line that passes through the two Terminal-class stations in Terracept at the same time (Terracept and Austrumcept).

Description []

Skyward Line is one of the District lines of Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division. It runs in Sava Threeler Sub-District and is mainly used to serve Mayler Airport nearby.

This route is represented by Blue on the Nazca Railway Route Map, and will be Line Number 6A.

Currently, this route is 3.56 km long, with a total of 4 stations.

Districts Served[]

  • Sava
    • Threeler

History[]

Development Chapters[]

  • S4E1: Jayler - Mayler Airport 1
  • S4E2: Jayler - Mayler Airport 2

Line Characteristics[]

  • One of the Branch Lines of Nazca Railway Los Sengas Division.
  • It is the second line opened in S4 and it is also the second line connecting to Mayler Airport.

Fun Facts[]

  • This line was originally named Avgto Line during the planning stages.
  • This line completes construction along all stations involved before connecting its tracks in a fashion similar to Expo Line.
  • All stations along this line are interchanges. This arrangement is also seen at Snowty Line after S4E5 and until S4E8, and Ingress Line until S4E6.

SLT Line 101 is a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas Downtown (Fare Zone 1). This line has 10 stops, and runs between Metropolis Estate and South Bay NR Station.

Contents

  • 1 Description
  • 2 History
  • 3 List of Stations
  • 4 Rolling Stock
  • 5 Gallery
  • 6 Citations and References

Description[]

SLT Line 101 mainly serves the Metropolis Sub-District in Downtown, and is currently 3.25 km long.

This line is Line Number 101 in the SLT system, and is represented by Orange (The representative color of Downtown Fare Zone).

History[]

  • January 20 2016: This line was established.
  • April 8 2018: This line extended to East Stadium Path.
  • October 23 2020: This line extended to Red Stadium South.
  • March 23 2022: This line extended to South Bay NR Station.

SLT Line 102 is a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas Downtown (Fare Zone 1). This line currently has 3 stops, and runs between One Origin and Origin Court.

Contents

  • 1 Description
  • 2 History
  • 3 Future Development
  • 4 List of Stations
  • 5 Rolling Stock
  • 6 Gallery
  • 7 Citations and References

Description[]

SLT Line 102 mainly serves the southeast area of Downtown.

This line is Line Number 102 in the SLT system, and is represented by Orange (The representative color of Downtown Fare Zone).

History[]

  • Unknown: This line was established with two stops as the connecting line between two housing properties in Origin.
  • August 15 2022: This line extended to Origin Court.

Future Development[]

  • This line will extend to the High Approach area in Downtown, running in parallel with Line 103 between Origin NR Station and Decennial College, and Line 210 between On King and On Shun Street in the process.

SLT Line 103 is a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas Downtown (Fare Zone 1). This line currently has 10 stops, and runs between Atlantic Christian Church and Ringcrown.

Contents

  • 1 Description
  • 2 History
  • 3 List of Stations
  • 4 Rolling Stock
  • 5 Gallery
  • 6 Citations and References

Description[]

SLT Line 103 mainly serves the northeast area of Downtown, and is currently 2.3 km long.

This line is Line Number 103 in the SLT system, and is represented by Orange (The representative color of Downtown Fare Zone).

History[]

  • October 11 2020: This line was established.
  • March 18 2021: This line extended to San Tin (North).
  • July 30 2022: This line extended to Decennial College.
  • August 16 2022: This line extended to Ringcrown.
  • January 25 2023: Caca Road is added on this line.

SLT Line 104 is a line operated by Sava Light Transit between Los Sengas Downtown (Fare Zone 1) and Sava (Fare Zone 2). This line currently has 12 stops, and runs between Metro Stone NR Station and Kofu Street.

Contents

  • 1 Description
  • 2 Fun Facts
  • 3 History
  • 4 List of Stations
  • 5 Rolling Stock
  • 6 Gallery
  • 7 Citations and References

Description[]

SLT Line 104 mainly serves the northwest area of Downtown and briefly enters Sava.

This line is Line Number 104 in the SLT system, and is represented by Orange (The representative color of Downtown Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • At the section after Osaka Road, this line enters a circular single-track section that runs in parallel with Line 211. However, while Line 211 runs in the counter-clockwise direction in the circular section, this line runs in the clockwise direction in that section.

History[]

  • February 15 2021: This line copmleted construction.
  • May 21 2021: Sapporo Street and Shizuoka Street began operations.

SLT Line 1511 is a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas TriPaw (Fare Zone 15).This line currently has 5 stops, and runs between Old Brightland Central and Yin Lam.

Contents

  • 1 Description
  • 2 Fun Facts
  • 3 List of Stations
  • 4 Rolling Stock
  • 5 Gallery
  • 6 Citations and References

Description[]

SLT Line 1511 runs along the east of TriPaw Continent.

This line is Line Number 1511 in the SLT system, and is represented by Milky White (The representative color of TriPaw Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • The entirety of this line runs in parallel with Line 1514. However, while it is confirmed that this line will split with Line 1514 after stopping at Yin Lam and would go on to Anjou, the section after Yin Lam is not built yet.

SLT Line 1512 is a proposed line of Sava Light Transit.

Contents

  • 2 Fun Facts
  • 3 List of Stations
  • 4 Rolling Stock
  • 5 Gallery
  • 6 Citations and References

Description []

SLT Line 1512 will serve the northeast TriPaw.

This line will be Line Number 1512 in the SLT system, and will be represented by Milky White (The representative color of TriPaw Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • While this line has yet to be established, the platform structure for 5 of the stops in this line (Old Brightland Central, Harisa, University East Gate, Kwong Fuk Park, St. Louis), as well as their connecting tunnels, have already been built. However, as the tracks have not been connected, this line is still seen as a proposed line.

SLT Line 1514 is a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas TriPaw (Fare Zone 15).This line currently has 9 stops, and runs between Old Brightland Central and Ling Ha Street.

Contents

  • 1 Description
  • 2 Fun Facts
  • 3 List of Stations
  • 4 Rolling Stock
  • 5 Gallery
  • 6 Citations and References

Description[]

SLT Line 1514 runs along between the northeast and the east of Tripaw Peninsula.

This line is Line Number 1514 in the SLT system, and is represented by Milky White (The representative color of TriPaw Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • This section between Old Brightland Central and Yin Lam of this line runs in parallel with Line 1511.

Description []

SLT Line 1516 will serve TriPaw.

This line will be Line Number 1516 in the SLT system, and will be represented by Milky White (The representative color of TriPaw Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • While this line has yet to be established, reserved platforms for this line are seen at Old Brightland Central.

SLT Line 1521 is a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas TriPaw (Fare Zone 15). This line currently has 8 stops, and runs between Hiu Lai Court I and Dominic Road.

  • 1 Description
  • 2 Fun Facts

Description[]

SLT Line 1521 runs along the center of Tripaw Peninsula.

This line is Line Number 1521 in the SLT system, and is represented by Milky White (The representative color of TriPaw Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • This line has plans to extend from both ends in the future.

SLT Line 1601 was a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas Yowah (Fare Zone 16). At the time of its operation, this line had 2 stops, namely Prosand and Jadesand Estate, with two additional stops that were planned but were never constructed.

Contents

  • 2 List of Stations
  • 3 Rolling Stock
  • 4 Gallery
  • 5 Citations and References

Description[]

SLT Line 1601 ran along the east of Yowah.

This line was Line Number 1601 in the SLT system, and was represented by Apricot (The representative color of Yowah Fare Zone).

Description []

SLT Line 1701 is a line that runs between the Nail Bight and Monley Coast vicinities in Cometsilk.

This line is Line Number 1701 in the SLT system, and is represented by Blue (The representative color of Cometsilk Fare Zone).

SLT Line 1901 is a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas Internal Sea (Fare Zone 19). It circles Shore Tip in a figure-eight pattern, and has 10 stops.

Contents

  • 1 Description
  • 2 Fun Facts
  • 3 List of Stations
  • 4 Rolling Stock
  • 5 Citations and References

Description[]

SLT Line 1901 is a circular line that runs between the east and west of Shore Tip in Internal Sea.

This line is Line Number 1901 in the SLT system, and is represented by Dark Blue (The representative color of Internal Sea Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • This line runs in a "figure-eight" pattern within Shore Tip, and is the first SLT line, as well as the first railway line in Los Sengas to operate in such a behavior. This may explain the reason why, despite being a circular line, this line does not have a letter "L" appended to the line number.
  • Despite being a circular line, this line has two tracks. This makes it the first dual-track circular line in the SLT system.
  • The full circle of this line involves passing through Maai Ping twice.

SLT Line 1902 is a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas Internal Sea (Fare Zone 19). It runs between Shore Tip and Tooth Cliff, and currently has 10 stops.

Description[]

SLT Line 1902 is a line that runs between the southwest and north of Shore Tip in Internal Sea.

This line is Line Number 1902 in the SLT system, and is represented by Dark Blue (The representative color of Internal Sea Fare Zone).

SLT Line 1903 is a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas Internal Sea (Fare Zone 19). It runs between Bowplate River and Lau Zeng, and currently has 6 stops.

Contents

  • 1 Description
  • 2 Fun Facts
  • 3 List of Stations
  • 4 Rolling Stock
  • 5 Citations and References

Description[]

SLT Line 1903 is a line that runs along the east coast of Shore Tip in Internal Sea.

This line is Line Number 1903 in the SLT system, and is represented by Dark Blue (The representative color of Internal Sea Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • This line is not connnected to the other two SLT lines in Internal Sea (Line 1901, Line 1902) by track.

SLT Line 1L is a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas Downtown (Fare Zone 1). It circles Metropolis (Sub-District) in a counter-clockwise direction, and has 18 stops.

Contents

  • 1 Description
  • 2 Fun Facts
  • 3 History
  • 4 List of Stations
  • 5 Rolling Stock
  • 6 Gallery
  • 7 Citations and References

Description[]

SLT Line 1L mainly serves the Metropolis Sub-District in Downtown, and is currently 6.91 km long.

This line is Line Number 1L in the SLT system, and is represented by Orange (The representative color of Downtown Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • Due to the circular nature of this line, unlike most other SLT lines, this line only has a single track.
  • At the section between Metropolis (Phase III) and Metropolis (Phase II), the route of this line is built directly above the large-scaled Nazca Railway Route map despite being underground. Due to the fact that this section is supported by overhanging pillars, it can be considered as a 'pseudo-overground' section.

History[]

  • January 20 2016: This line was established.
  • October 12 2020: This line extended northwards to Metro Stone.
  • October 15 2020: After 4 years, this line formed a complete ring.
  • May 17 2021: San Annis Stadium Main Gate Stop begun operations.
  • September 13 2022: Origin NR Station Stop begun operations.
  • October 2 2022: Exit E3 was added in Nazca Railway Origin Station to connect to Origin NR Station Stop.

Description[]

SLT Line 2001 is a circular line that runs along the city center of Egress.

This line is Line Number 2001 in the SLT system, and is represented by Light Brown (The representative color of Egress Fare Zone)..

SLT Line 2002 is a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas Egress (Fare Zone 20). It currently has four stops.

Contents

  • 1 Description
  • 2 Fun Facts
  • 3 List of Stations
  • 4 Rolling Stock
  • 5 Citations and References

Description[]

SLT Line 2002 runs at the southwest of Egress.

This line is Line Number 2002 in the SLT system, and is represented by Light Brown (The representative color of Egress Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • This line will extend to Northwest River Rendezvous in the future.

SLT Line 2003 is a proposed line of Sava Light Transit.

Contents

  • 1 Description 
  • 2 Fun Facts
  • 3 Rolling Stock
  • 4 Gallery
  • 5 Citations and References

Description []

SLT Line 2003 will serve Egress.

This line will be Line Number 2003 in the SLT system, and will be represented by Light Brown (The representative color of Egress Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • While this line has yet to be established, reserved platforms for this line are seen at River Rendezvous Stop.
  • This line will serve southwest Egress in the future, in particular the Occupy Corner, Mount Egress, and the Star Gate areas.

Rolling Stock[]

Line 2003 will use Minecart throughout.

SLT Line 2004 is a proposed line of Sava Light Transit.

Contents

  • 1 Description 
  • 2 Fun Facts
  • 3 Rolling Stock
  • 4 Gallery
  • 5 Citations and References

Description []

SLT Line 2004 will serve Egress.

This line will be Line Number 2004 in the SLT system, and will be represented by Light Brown (The representative color of Egress Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • Reserved platforms for this line were seen at the old River Rendezvous Stop alongside Line 2003. However, following the reconstruction of River Rendezvous Stop on March 5 2026, the fate of this line becomes unknown as two of the reserved platforms are demolished in the new station.

Rolling Stock[]

Line 2004 will use Minecart throughout.

SLT Line 201 is a line operated by Sava Light Transit within Los Sengas Sava (Fare Zone 2). This line has 14 stops, and runs between Sava Bay Bus Terminal and Vincere Road NR Station.

Contents

  • 1 Description
  • 2 Fun Facts
  • 3 History
  • 4 List of Stations
  • 5 Rolling Stock
  • 6 Gallery
  • 7 Citations and References

Description[]

SLT Line 201 mainly serves The Three Pass and Sava Canyon in Sava.

This line is Line Number 201 in the SLT system, and is represented by Purple (The representative color of Sava Fare Zone).

Fun Facts[]

  • At the section after Sava Bay Road South, this line enters a circular single-track section that runs in parallel with Line 202. However, while Line 202 runs in the clockwise direction in the circular section, this line runs in the counter-clockwise direction in that section.

History[]

  • May 16 2020: The Three Pass Bay Stop was demolished.
  • January 10 2021: The section between Mars Street and Vincere Road NR Station began services.
